newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Power NZ issues Utilicorp placement notice.
newsitem.headline: Power NZ issues Utilicorp placement notice.

text.p: Power New Zealand Ltd said on Thursday that following Utilicorp's failure to remedy its breaches of the cornerstone Relationship Deed, Power NZ had issued a notice triggering a deemed transfer notice in respect of Utilicorp's shareholding in Power NZ.

"In terms of the Cornerstone Relationship Deed, the directors now have the right to place Utilicorp's shares with a party whom they consider to be a suitable shareholder," Power NZ said in a statement.
No decision had yet been made in that respect, it said.
Utilicorp last week issued proceedings to stop Power NZ from exercising these rights.
Power NZ said the hearing for the injunction would take place at the High Court on August 1.

"Power NZ is looking forward to the matter being determined quickly, so that shareholders can be fully informed about the underlying ownership of the company prior to its annual meeting on 11 September," it said.

Utilicorp New Zealand, controlled by U.S. power company Utilicorp United Inc, said last week it planned to challenge legal moves by Power NZ's independent directors, which it feared could delay its plans for a joint takeover.

Utilicorp and local unlisted power company Mercury Energy plan to pool their respective shareholdings in electricity distributor Power NZ in order to take shared, 64 percent control through a joint venture.
Although the plan has been cleared by monopolies authorities, independent directors of Power NZ started legal action relating to a long-standing cornerstone agreement with Utilicorp.

Utilicorp has said the joint venture plan will only take effect if the cornerstone relationship is terminated. Both it and Mercury believe that the agreement no longer adds value to Power NZ and should be ended. Utilicorp has said it had legal advice that its joint venture plan did not breach the agreement.
